title: Doesn’t fix issues, just adds new features
body:
I am a long term user. I have been using it everyday since January 2021. I have even bought the premium version of the app. 

This app has really helped me with my life. I highly recommend this app to anyone wanting a track their habits. However, I would not recommend this app to use long-term as if you want to track your progress, you can’t as I have explained below. 

I initially reviewed and rated it 5*. The reason why I am rating it 1* is because, as time went by, the habit tracking became more and more broken, unstable, unusable meaning that if you go on any specific habit, then you scroll down to ‘trending’ or ‘comparison’ between weeks, months and years. It doesn’t show last weeks or this weeks / last month or this month / last year or this years progress. Instead, it’s just a blank black screen. This has been like this for 6-9 months and I thought that I would give the developers the opportunities to fix this issue however they did not fix the issue but instead of pushing out new features and updates rather than fixing the original issue. 

This is unfair for the people who has paid for the premium service, but isn’t getting the basic features of the app.

I have increased my review from 1* to 3*. I feel like this app was really good in 2021 but has been going downhill ever since then. The 1 good feature is the integration of external apps like Apple health like when you do a certain activity or meditation, it automatically counts in the habit tracking app rather than manually putting in the values.

title: Lack of inclusivity
body:
I was quite disappointed to see a lack of inclusivity when I clicked the icons tab. I normally prefer them over emojis due to aesthetics. But I noticed a lack of pills/medicine options, pet options, and I also noticed a lack of religious options. There were only Christianity and Judaism. If we go by ‘fastest growing religion logic’ or even abrahamic religions, Islam should have been included as well. But there is no moon and star, no mosques or tasbeehs which would’ve been really cute.

I had intended to use this app for general life alongside health. I have a poor working memory so I wanted to cover all aspects from health to education to my religious betterment and separate my pets additional care I.e alternating meds and my own medication but due to the lacking icons, it doesn’t really appeal to me anymore (I’m really particular about this.)

More so than this, the lack of anything pertaining to Islam makes me feel as though this app has a target audience and excludes me from this audience as using a church does not feel appropriate when I put in a religious habit - whilst it may still be useful for some things, it doesn’t cover everything I had hoped to track.

I would appreciate it if the icons could be updated to include more and to be categorised a little more as the current categories are general and lump quite a lot together. I had paid for premium before noticing this flaw and have been considering cancelling and looking for another app that meets everything due to thjs lack of inclusivity.

title: Can improve
body:
I have been using two features over the past six months of so - timing the habits daily and checking the stats. 

There’re too many excess features that are not useful and some are even dangerous. Moods and tips for example are redundant. What can really improve is the separation of adding/deleting habits from recording and timing them. The frequency of onboarding a new habit or editing an existing one is much lower than maintaining daily records. Therefore it makes more sense to put an extra layer of protection for the user to change the configuration of the habits. For example, I accidentally deleted a habit twice when I intended to clean record for the day. I ended up losing all the historic data.

I like the app since it has the feature that I can’t find in other apps, which made it unique. But that said, it’s not as reliable as my calendar after having my data so easily wiped out.

This is a well intentioned feedback. Well done in bringing the timing feature and pretty widgets in life.

title: Easy to use and great layout
body:
I love this app. I’ve been using it for a few weeks as I struggle to remember to take medications, but it’s also helpful for tracking other things. I like that you can track both daily habits, and also habits that you only need to do a few times per week/month. 

I also like that there are different units - for example, I track my water in ml, my breathing meditation in minutes, and my medication is a simple checklist of once per day. Also, the app allows pre-set values for things like water, so you can just click the “500ml” button rather than typing in a value every single time!

They also offer scholarships to the premium version of the app which I was fortunate enough to receive, which means that for those that can’t pay you can still have access to the premium version. 

And finally, the layout is simple but beautiful. Clean and easy to understand, but also has bright colours which I love. 

10/10, I have absolutely no notes - I love this app and use it all the time.

title: Fantastic Tool for ADHD
body:
As someone with ADHD, I know how hard it can be to stick to a habit. I'm always starting new things, but I rarely have the follow-through to make them stick. That's why Habit Tracker is so great. 

This app has everything I need to track my habits and stay motivated. I can create different types of habits, set reminders, and track my progress over time. I can also group habits with people I care about, which helps me stay accountable.

One of the things I love most about Habit Tracker is the customizability. I can set different reminder sounds, choose from a variety of widgets, and even use a focus timer for time-related habits. The home widgets are useful for tracking throughout the day too. 

There is a small fee but if you’re struggling please contact them as they will be able to support you with access to the app for free at their discretion.

Overall, Habit Tracker is a great app for people with(/without) ADHD who want to build and maintain healthy habits. It's easy to use, customizable, and packed with features that can help you stay on track. I highly recommend it!

title: Definitely good overall
body:
First off - this is a really good app and I’ve already noticed a difference in personal accountability for the habits I’m trying to create. It’s easy to add in the tasks you e completed and the widget, UI and colours are really nice as well as the flexibility in reminder times and you don’t have to connect to a smart watch to track fitness goals as you can add sessions manually. 
I paid for premium as I wanted to add more habits and it’s not expensive at all for the benefits.  

Main gripes: 
If you choose a habit to be “any x days in a week, or a month” it shows that habit every day. But, because it shows every day if I haven’t done it that day (but plan to do the following) then your stats won’t show as 100% for that day (even if I do end up completing over the course of a week) which is a little disheartening for tracking progress as shows incomplete days that are complete. Also the fact if you edit anything about the habit such as frequency it deletes all the data for that habit so you lose your stats and the “mass check in” didn’t actually log for me. 

For the price though, it’s great app and I’d recommend it, but for new users just be aware you’re better setting your habits to set days for better tracking and you’ll be good to go 👌🏻

title: This app saved my life
body: Thank you so much to the creator of this app, please never change anything about it. I spent years rotting in bed and depressed, feeling like I am lazy and useless and my life was out of control, I’ve tried so many habit apps and they all didn’t help but that layout of this app is amazing and makes me do things I need to do. Even if you want the premium (which isn’t forced on you) it is not super expensive. This app was created with women in mind, it’s aesthetically pleasing and so user friendly oh my God. They’ve thought of everything, being able to set reminders at specific times in the day, using emojis and a whole colour wheel for tasks, assigning different tasks for different days, tons of weekly and daily and monthly charts and breakdowns of your progress, it’s amazing. It makes me want to get out of bed and believe in myself and out of this mental health rut. Even if you need help doing the small things like brushing your teeth you can do it on here or big things like going to work, it works for both. This app alongside the “todo” app which lets you put your to do list as a sticky note on your Home Screen of your phone, have saved my Uni experience. I have so much motivation and hope for the future now, I’m so sad I didn’t find it sooner when I had all the motivation at night but none in the morning when I woke up. Now using this app I’m motivated all day and it feels like a fun game, life feels very doable, once I felt like I was failing at everything and achieving nothing and now I feel like even doing the smallest task in conquering the world. Thank you again!

- allow tracking habits without repetitions - e.g. I want to track how many times something happened today. Like a negative I simply want to register and watch over time. Otherwise an amazing app without annual subscription.

Happy habitting.

title: Absolutely love this app 💗 1% daily improvements here I come 🙌🏼
body:
After reading the book Atomic Habits by James Clear, the author states that by creating solid, workable, resistant free, simple systems for things you wish to change, then repeated daily will result in lasting and deep rooted habit change, don’t focus on the actual goal, focus on the small daily achievements and a 1% improvement each day towards that goal. 
So I went on the search for a good app with a visual tracker to keep me accountable for those 1% daily improvements. I absolutely love this app 💗 it’s so simple to use, it’s customisable for any habit you wish to add to your daily routine, you can add icons and emojis, titles, motivational reminders, set time goals, tick off with ease when you have done the task you wanted to achieve for the day and then review how you’ve done over various time periods, it give you analysis data to view and after having it for just 1 week so far I have achieved so much more then in the last two months of on/off procrastination. 
Think about the small wins you want to repeat daily towards the changes you want to make in your life and the habits you want to form ie running, making your bed, drinking water, no alcohol....anything and use this app as a motivational tool to track your progress, it won’t do the actual tasks for you of course but you can see visually your progress and you won’t want to break your running streak once you gain momentum...totally love this app and it’s really been a helpful tool to get me thinking and more importantly going, I highly recommend 🙌🏼 thank you app developer and please keep this going.

title: Baffling interface & unresponsive ‘back’ button
body:
Tried to change the time of a reminder: not obvious how to do that at first because its not on the page you go to if you click ‘edit’ (turns out its buried on another page you get to if you click ‘next’ at the very bottom of the page you get to from ‘edit’). Didn’t work that out initially so deleted the habit and tried to create it again with a correct reminder time. Appeared to succeed but then that habit was not visible under today’s list of habits. Eventually found out on the all habits page (presumably because the reminder time is now passed, though again that  isn’t immediately obvious) but again, it took a search to work that out. 

The ‘back’ button in the top left of the screen also often has to be repeatedly hit before it responds. This seems to be a not uncommon iPhone issue — I’ve seen it on two different iPhone 11s with far-corner buttons, on different apps — but still. 

Hopefully the non-intuitive interface is that way because they are rethinking habit lists in some clever way that is unlike other lists and so eventually I’ll appreciate the way it is. Maybe Apple will sort out the corner button issue too some day. On that basis, rather than my initial experience: 4 stars
